issues.description: Method name inconsistency for the same conceptual operation: the problem statement (problem_statement.md) uses the snake_case name `get_total_number_of_students()` while the UML in the problem statement and all code artifacts (template comments and the solution implementation) use the camelCase name `getTotalNumberOfStudents()`. Files/lines: problem_statement.md (line 40-41) contains the text "get_total_number_of_students()", while the UML entry in problem_statement.md (line 70) shows `getTotalNumberOfStudents()`. The template Lecture.java comment (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 12) and the solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 75) both refer to/implement `getTotalNumberOfStudents()`. This naming mismatch can confuse students about the exact method name to implement and may cause failing tests or compilation errors if they follow the snake_case form instead of the camelCase Java convention used by the provided code and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Replace the snake_case occurrence `get_total_number_of_students()` in problem_statement.md (lines 40-41) with the camelCase `getTotalNumberOfStudents()` to match the UML, template comments, and solution implementation. Alternatively, add a short clarifying note in problem_statement.md stating that `get_total_number_of_students()` in the text refers to the Java method `getTotalNumberOfStudents()` and that students should implement the camelCase name to match Java conventions and the provided code/tests.
